lede: Apple's record September quarter and a rebound in its shares lead the day, Singapore's Parliament has passed a tougher haze law, and the US midterm result is already rippling through AI and data-centre news. Singapore's AI startup section is short today, with only two stories in the last 72 hours that I could confirm.
stocks_note: Latest closes: New York, Wednesday 4 November (AAPL, GOOGL) and SGX, Wednesday 4 November (DBS), via Yahoo Finance. Apple reported its fiscal fourth quarter on 2 November; no upcoming earnings dates seen for the three.

sections.title: Apple
sections.subtitle: Official news in brief, then 9to5Mac and MacRumors

official.label: From Apple
official.summary: Apple posted fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent and a September-quarter record, with iPhone and Services both at highs. It declared a 27-cent dividend. Separately, the redesigned Health app, now in the iOS 27.3 beta, adds Insights and Longevity tabs and more languages, and reaches everyone later this year.

items.headline: Siri AI no longer needs a waitlist, except at busy times
items.summary: An updated Apple support page says the waitlist used to gate Siri AI when it launched in iOS 27 this autumn has been dropped. The one exception is periods of unusually high demand, when Apple may still hold some people back.

items.headline: Apple Music gets two upgrades in the iOS 27.3 beta
items.summary: The first iOS 27.3 beta arrived this week, and 9to5Mac has found two changes to Apple Music inside it. The update is still in testing, so details may shift before it reaches the public later on.

items.headline: Apple is trimming employee AI spending
items.summary: Bloomberg reports Apple cut some engineers' daily AI allowance from $300 to $200 in October, with $100 possible next. Some teams may be capped at $25 and asked to use cheaper or on-device models. Staff can request more from executives.

items.headline: Apple will scan public iCloud links for harmful content from iOS 27.3
items.summary: Photos and files shared with an Anyone-with-the-link setting will be made available to Apple for a check. Apple does not define harmful content, and says it may remove it and act against the account of anyone uploading it.

items.headline: Parliament passes tougher haze law after six-hour debate
items.summary: MPs backed amendments that raise the maximum fine to S$20 million and give authorities more tools against firms tied to overseas fires. Grace Fu said investigations into four 2015 notices stay open, and three of those firms are implicated in this year's haze.

items.headline: Rena Lee elected to the International Court of Justice
items.summary: Singapore's Ambassador for International Law won in the first round, with 151 of 191 General Assembly votes and 13 of 15 in the Security Council. She is the first Singaporean on the court and only the second from South-east Asia. Her nine-year term starts in 2027.

items.headline: Islamic college funding will not squeeze other community needs
items.summary: Zaqy Mohamad told Parliament that Muis will keep balancing support for the Singapore College of Islamic Studies against mosques, madrasahs and aid for low-income families, even if zakat is used. The college takes its first students in 2028.

items.headline: Bin rummagers may get an advisory, not a fine
items.summary: Grace Fu said in a written reply that officers may simply advise people found going through public bins for containers when no litter is left behind. Enforcement is case by case, with a focus on education, and those in need can be referred to social agencies.

items.headline: British man to be charged over hidden camera on Japan-Singapore flight
items.summary: Police say the 52-year-old planted a camera in a plane toilet and started it from his phone. A crew member found it, and he allegedly deleted the app and photos afterwards. He faces voyeurism and obstruction charges on 5 November.

items.headline: Cabinet backs Rs 2,814 crore push for critical mineral processing
items.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a scheme to build domestic processing of minerals such as lithium and nickel, aiming to cut import dependence. It is part of India's wider effort to secure supplies for batteries and clean energy.

items.headline: Cyclone Murasu drenches Telangana's Bhadradri and Khammam
items.summary: One mandal each in Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem got 204 to 235 mm of rain overnight into 4 November, after red alerts the day before. An orange alert stayed for Bhadradri that day, with yellow for Khammam and Mulugu.

items.headline: Blast damages railway line in Rajasthan, sabotage probed
items.summary: A powerful explosion on Tuesday night damaged the Anupgarh-Suratgarh track near 50 GB village in Sriganganagar, shattering sleepers and pillars. A passenger train had passed shortly before. Multi-agency teams are investigating and four trains were cancelled.

items.headline: Bihar to fill more than 11,000 health department posts
items.summary: The state health society says the formal notification should come by the last week of November, with a recruitment calendar to follow. The roles are administrative, technical and medical support, and the process is expected to take six to seven months.

items.headline: High Court tells schools to tackle bullying over gender identity
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court issued directions while hearing a petition from the mother of a 16-year-old Faridabad student who died. It said schools must address bullying based on gender identity and sexual orientation.

items.headline: Republicans blame Trump after midterm defeat
items.summary: Some Republicans told the BBC the president's focus on his legacy and indifference to voter worries cost the party dearly. One called the result a disaster, after a Democratic wave in Tuesday's midterm elections.

items.headline: Canada sees midterm result as a lever for tariff relief
items.summary: With US-Canada trade talks back on, Tuesday's Democratic wave puts pressure on the White House to strike a deal. Canadians hoping for relief from tariffs are reading the outcome as a win.

items.headline: Ukraine releases bodycam footage of deadly double-tap strike
items.summary: Kyiv says the video shows a Russian bombing that hit rescuers after an initial strike on a village on Monday. At least 40 people were killed and about 30 more may still be under the rubble.

items.headline: Hackers hit freezers used to store blood in France
items.summary: The French Blood Establishment says cold rooms holding blood were affected by the attacks. Theories about who is responsible are circulating, and the incident has raised questions about the security of health infrastructure.

items.headline: Israel's president opens talks after election deadlock
items.summary: Isaac Herzog began consultations with party leaders and warned that not every promise can be kept if they want to avoid another election. The vote left no clear route to a governing coalition.

brief.summary: IMDA is working with GoDaddy, Infoblox, Cloudflare and Google to test whether the domain name system can identify and verify AI agents, while GovTech builds an internal agent registry for public agencies. Separately, Databricks has opened a bigger Singapore office tied to a US$350 million investment, and Tencent Cloud showed new AI tools at its Singapore event.

sections.title: Singapore AI startups
sections.subtitle: Funding, hiring, and what they're building

items.headline: Databricks opens bigger Singapore office and a startup accelerator
items.summary: The data and AI firm opened its new regional office and plans to invest US$350 million in Singapore over three years, taking its local team from about 250 to more than 500. A startup accelerator aims to back over 100 early-stage companies over three years.

items.headline: Featherless to offer MiniMax M3.1 Flash for coding
items.summary: Singapore-based Featherless, which hosts open-weight models behind a single API, says it will add MiniMax's M3.1 Flash. The model has 428 billion parameters in total, with 23 billion active for each token, and is aimed at coding work.

items.headline: Meta buys AI coding startup Conductor
items.summary: Conductor lets software engineers run teams of AI agents on different parts of a project at the same time. Meta's purchase adds a multi-agent coding tool to its developer-focused AI push. Terms were not given in the report.

items.headline: Only four people booked an Uber through an AI agent in its busiest week
items.summary: Uber told investors that agent-made bookings were tiny last quarter, a reality check for the idea that chatbots will take over how people hail rides. The company is watching for risks of being squeezed out as middleman.

items.headline: AI industry PACs spent millions on the midterms, with mixed results
items.summary: Political groups funded by the AI industry tried to shape who sits in Congress this cycle and had a mixed scorecard. They are already looking ahead to the next election.

items.headline: Data-centre backlash was a theme of the midterms
items.summary: Opposition to new data centres drove many battleground races and dozens of local ballot measures. The result suggests that building AI infrastructure may face tougher local politics from here.

items.headline: Qualcomm bets on data centres as phone sales sink
items.summary: Qualcomm expects data-centre chips to eventually make up about 30 percent of its business, as its smartphone sales weaken. The earnings update shows another chipmaker leaning on AI demand.

items.headline: Tencent releases Hy4, its flagship open-weight model
items.summary: Hy4 is aimed at agent tasks inside Tencent's enterprise software, and handles images for the first time, reading charts and doing visual maths. It enters a crowded open-weight field with DeepSeek, Z.ai and Alibaba.

items.headline: DeepSeek engineer defends open-source push toward AGI
items.summary: Speaking at the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen, DeepSeek's Gao Xi said openness speeds shared progress even if it raises safety risks. He was responding to concern in the US and some scrutiny in China about national security.

items.headline: Joe Tsai calls open source the only sustainable path for AI
items.summary: Alibaba's chairman told the Wuzhen Summit that open ecosystems are the way to build a lasting AI industry, as Alibaba doubles down on open-source models despite US pushback.

items.headline: Baidu builds an AI simulator to train robotaxis on rare hazards
items.summary: The tool recreates unusual road events, such as a cyclist running a red light or an animal darting out, to prepare Apollo robotaxis for them. Baidu hopes it gives an edge in the fast-growing self-driving taxi market.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing exposes a profit gap with Z.ai and MiniMax
items.summary: The prospectus Anthropic filed with the SEC last week shows a far bigger financial cushion than its closest Chinese rivals, whose models keep improving. It highlights how hard it is for them to turn technical gains into a sustainable business.
